name: Pixel art: a 16-colour palette, whole pixels, stepped time
for: games, retro and 8-bit topics, developer humour, anything that should read as a screen from 1990; a scene drawn at a small size and shown at an integer scale, or footage turned into pixel art with pixelate.py

motion.ease: none: positions are whole logical pixels and time is held on whole animation frames (on twos or threes); no easing curves, no motion blur
motion.note: on twos: 12 drawings a second in a 24 fps video (or 8 on threes, 6 on fours; at 30 fps use 15, 10 or 6). A walk is 6 to 8 frames at 80 to 125 ms; a hit freezes the world for 0.15 to 0.25 s (fighting games hold 9 to 14 frames at 60 fps), then shakes by 2 to 4 pixels with a fast decay

camera: cuts, and pans in whole pixels; a shake is a few pixels for a few frames

texture.note: no grain, no gradients, no blur: ordered (Bayer) dither where a gradient is wanted, never error diffusion

avoid: rotating or scaling a finished sprite

sound.mood: chiptune: square and triangle waves, a noise snare, short arpeggios

source: ours. The palette is PICO-8's sixteen colours; the sizes are multiples of one logical pixel at scale 6 (8 px = 0.044 of the height, 16 px = 0.089)
